Part of organized koala search Waite campus by csiro staff

Our team consisted of myself, Gabriel Bucco, and Jeff Kelley, all working on the CSIRO Waite campus. Exchanged my low-res iPhone image for Gabriel's (who was standing next to me) high-res photo taken with a telephoto lens. Gabriel wondered whether the true location of the tree we looked in was several meters NE (up & right) of the location recorded by the iPhone app (within the error of GPS) given the surrounding landmarks. Summary: Very enjoyable! I've only previously seen one other Koala in the Waite arboretum this year, i.e. since I started working at CSIRO.

Multiple photos submitted and overall location of koalas submitted.

I returned to the site an hour or so later and confirmed that the koala in the photo was a male as the genitalia were clearly visible - he had moved to a branch in the tree and was reclining in a fork.   More photos taken.  Koalas are not infrequently seen in the Waite Arboretum.  Usually they are in the sugar gums along Claremont Avenue or in the northwest corner where this one was recorded.  Koalas are more numerous in the Waite Conservation Reserve - grey box woodland.

Found during survey of 147 ha Waite Conservation Reserve by 19 surveyors in 13 groups who cumulatively spent about 30 hours and recorded 20 koalas (includes 6 submitted by Steve Marvanek via Phone App). Searching thus involved about 90 minutes per koala per person.
